titulo: Accusative and prepositions of place: Wo? × Wohin?: In, an, auf: where and where to

aula.titulo: Accusative and prepositions of place: Wo? × Wohin?
aula.objetivo: Use the prepositions that take the accusative (durch, für, gegen, ohne, um) and the nine two-way prepositions, choosing the dative (Wo?, no movement) or the accusative (Wohin?, with movement).

sessao.titulo: In, an, auf: where and where to

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: Compare the pairs. STEP 2: Notice these sentences too. STEP 3: Ich fahre mit dem Bus. STEP 4: Das Geschenk ist für dich. STEP 5: Ich gehe zum Arzt. STEP 6: Ich komme aus der Schule. Ich gehe ohne ihn. STEP 7: Questions: STEP 8: Which case appears with wo? And with wohin? STEP 9: After mit, aus and zu, which case follows? And after für and ohne? Zum is the merging of which two words?

tabela.c2: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.

tabela.c1: Die Lampe steht neben dem Bett.
tabela.c2: Ich stelle die Lampe neben das Bett.

blocos.titulo: The nine two-way prepositions: a regra de ouro
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: nine prepositions change case depending on the question: an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen. STEP 2: GOLDEN RULE: if the question is WO? (where, WITHOUT movement), use the DATIVE; if it is WOHIN? (where to, WITH movement), use the ACCUSATIVE. STEP 3: in this session, the three most common: «in» (in, inside), «an» (at, on a vertical surface, next to), «auf» (on, on top of). STEP 4: contractions: in dem = im; an dem = am; in das = ins; an das = ans; auf das = aufs. STEP 5: the article changes between the two cases in every gender: masculine Wo? «dem», Wohin? «den»; feminine: Wo? «der», Wohin? «die»; neuter: Wo? «dem», Wohin? «das». STEP 6: careful: «Ich bin im Garten» (state) × «Ich gehe in den Garten» (movement).
blocos.comparacao: English uses different words to show movement («in the garden» × «into the garden»). German uses the SAME preposition («in») and lets the case show whether there is movement.
